@morehao/dsh-github-trending.meta.description: Fetch GitHub Trending on a daily schedule, summarize it in Chinese, commit into your own repo and auto-merge the PR. All content is produced by the local trendradar core.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.meta.title: GitHub Trending Digest
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.allowDegraded: Allow falling back to original text when the model fails
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.allowDegraded.help: When on, if the model call for one repo fails its original-text summary is used as a fallback, so a single failure does not abort the whole digest. When off, any failure fails the whole run.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.credential.directHint: Resolved at run time from host credentials / env and passed straight to the core.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.credential.missingHint: Direct mode, but the ref is empty or unresolvable; use “Reuse DSH configuration” to refill it.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.credential.proxyHint: The loopback proxy forwards with the host credential; the key never passes through the plugin. Nothing to fill in here.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.maxTokens.help: Upper bound on tokens per model reply. Too low may truncate the summary; too high consumes more quota. Set it to fit the summary length you need.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.quickfill.desc: Reads the host provider catalog and credential state to fill endpoint, model and key source. Keys stay in memory.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.model.temperature.help: Sampling temperature, usually 0–2: lower is more stable and faithful to the source; higher is more varied. Around 0.3 works well for summaries.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.network.proxy.help: Outbound proxy for the core process (fetching GitHub Trending / pushing). GUI hosts often do not inherit the shell http(s)_proxy, so direct connections time out in some regions; e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890. Leave empty for no proxy.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.observe.backfillDays.help: How many days to backfill a first-seen repo from GitHub history (0 = no backfill, accumulate from today; max 365).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.observe.enabled.help: Records a daily star snapshot of candidate repos and derives "stars today" from local diffs instead of the trending-page number; turn it off to fall back to the old "increment only from the trending page" behaviour. Data lives in $DSH_HOME, never in the archive repo.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.observe.maxCandidates.help: Max candidate repos recorded per run (more = broader coverage and more requests; 300 ≈ 3 batch requests/day is recommended).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.last.noPreview: This run has no saved preview copy
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.live.note: The core fetches, summarizes, renders and commits in one run; there is no per-step progress before it finishes. Only elapsed time and a coarse phase are shown here.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.live.title: Running
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.ready.title: Readiness
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.releases.title: Subscriptions
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.tokens.note: The overview surfaces "how many tokens this run spent / all-time accumulated / how many new versions across subscribed repos"; total only, not split by dimension; this run total already includes the subscriptions stage. With an old core that has no data, the corresponding tile is hidden entirely, never shown as 0.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.tokens.title: Token usage
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.overview.week.title: Recent leaderboards
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.quickfill.hint: One click reuses the current DSH default model; expand to pick another configured provider and model if needed.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.direct: exportable key, passed to the core
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.missing: no usable credential, fill it in manually
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.proxy: credential not exportable, uses the loopback proxy
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.quickfill.title: Reuse a configured DSH model
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.backfillLatest.help: On the first check of a newly subscribed repo, summarize the latest N releases into the document as a starting point; 0 = no backfill (the first change analysis stays empty, only the baseline is recorded). Later runs diff incrementally as usual.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.budget.help: Overall budget for model calls in the subscriptions stage; “Auto” resolves by subscription count (min(300, 30 + 3×N)).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.card.hint: New releases of subscribed repos become Chinese summaries, committed to the same branch/PR as the board.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.card.title: Subscriptions stage
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.concurrency.help: How many repos to check at once; “Auto” resolves by subscription count (clamp(4, ceil(N/10), 8)).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.empty: Subscriptions were not enabled for this run
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.includeDrafts.help: Draft releases also count; drafts are only visible to tokens with write access.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.includePrerelease.help: Releases marked as pre-release on GitHub also count as new releases.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.notesChars.help: Truncate each release notes to this length to keep prompts bounded (500–20000).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.help: Check every subscribed repo for new releases at a fixed moment each week; independent of the board schedule.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.hint: Driven by the plugin’s own 60 s tick; a missed moment is caught up within 6 h once, and the same ISO week never runs twice (the core also has a week gate).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.title: Weekly check

@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summarize.batchSize.help: Repos per model call; larger batches run faster but make each prompt longer.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summarize.enrich.help: Adds external context before summarizing: repo fetches GitHub topics, readme also excerpts the README. Requires a read-only token.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summarize.enrichNote: Enrich needs a read-only token: enrich=repo/readme is best paired with GITHUB_READ_TOKEN (separate, read-only). In readme mode slow networks may skip some repos when the budget runs out (auto-degrades; the run is unaffected).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summarize.maxRetries.help: Extra retries per failed batch; 0 disables retry, and a batch that still fails follows the degrade policy.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summarize.readmeChars.help: Max README characters excerpted per repo when enrich=readme (longer text is truncated).
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summaryLang.coreTooOld: The current core is too old (requires ≥ 0.12.0); the summary language takes effect after upgrading the core. You can pick it now and it will apply once upgraded.
@morehao/dsh-github-trending.summaryLang.help: Language used for generated digests / release summaries. Follows the host UI language by default; anything other than Chinese/English falls back to Chinese. Requires core ≥ 0.12.0.

dsh-github-trending.observe.enabled.help: Records a daily star snapshot of candidate repos and derives "stars today" from local diffs instead of the trending-page number; turn it off to fall back to the old "increment only from the trending page" behaviour. Data lives in $DSH_HOME, never in the archive repo.
dsh-github-trending.observe.maxCandidates.help: Max candidate repos recorded per run (more = broader coverage and more requests; 300 ≈ 3 batch requests/day is recommended).
dsh-github-trending.overview.last.noPreview: This run has no saved preview copy
dsh-github-trending.overview.live.note: The core fetches, summarizes, renders and commits in one run; there is no per-step progress before it finishes. Only elapsed time and a coarse phase are shown here.
dsh-github-trending.overview.live.title: Running
dsh-github-trending.overview.ready.title: Readiness
dsh-github-trending.overview.releases.title: Subscriptions
dsh-github-trending.overview.tokens.note: The overview surfaces "how many tokens this run spent / all-time accumulated / how many new versions across subscribed repos"; total only, not split by dimension; this run total already includes the subscriptions stage. With an old core that has no data, the corresponding tile is hidden entirely, never shown as 0.
dsh-github-trending.overview.tokens.title: Token usage
dsh-github-trending.overview.week.title: Recent leaderboards
dsh-github-trending.quickfill.hint: One click reuses the current DSH default model; expand to pick another configured provider and model if needed.
dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.direct: exportable key, passed to the core
dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.missing: no usable credential, fill it in manually
dsh-github-trending.quickfill.mode.proxy: credential not exportable, uses the loopback proxy
dsh-github-trending.quickfill.title: Reuse a configured DSH model
dsh-github-trending.releases.backfillLatest.help: On the first check of a newly subscribed repo, summarize the latest N releases into the document as a starting point; 0 = no backfill (the first change analysis stays empty, only the baseline is recorded). Later runs diff incrementally as usual.
dsh-github-trending.releases.budget.help: Overall budget for model calls in the subscriptions stage; “Auto” resolves by subscription count (min(300, 30 + 3×N)).
dsh-github-trending.releases.card.hint: New releases of subscribed repos become Chinese summaries, committed to the same branch/PR as the board.
dsh-github-trending.releases.card.title: Subscriptions stage
dsh-github-trending.releases.concurrency.help: How many repos to check at once; “Auto” resolves by subscription count (clamp(4, ceil(N/10), 8)).
dsh-github-trending.releases.empty: Subscriptions were not enabled for this run
dsh-github-trending.releases.includeDrafts.help: Draft releases also count; drafts are only visible to tokens with write access.
dsh-github-trending.releases.includePrerelease.help: Releases marked as pre-release on GitHub also count as new releases.
dsh-github-trending.releases.notesChars.help: Truncate each release notes to this length to keep prompts bounded (500–20000).
dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.help: Check every subscribed repo for new releases at a fixed moment each week; independent of the board schedule.
dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.hint: Driven by the plugin’s own 60 s tick; a missed moment is caught up within 6 h once, and the same ISO week never runs twice (the core also has a week gate).
dsh-github-trending.releases.schedule.title: Weekly check
dsh-github-trending.restoreNotice.body: Quit DSH completely (⌘Q) and reopen it so the update takes effect.
dsh-github-trending.restoreNotice.title: Updated to v{version}
dsh-github-trending.run.error.title: Last error
dsh-github-trending.run.force.hint: Ignore the summary cache and re-fetch and re-summarize
dsh-github-trending.run.force.noChange: No content change; no new commit
dsh-github-trending.run.history.title: History
dsh-github-trending.run.last.title: Last result
dsh-github-trending.run.pendingPr.hint: Re-running the same day appends a commit and updates this PR; merged/closed records are cleaned up automatically.
dsh-github-trending.run.usage.tokensNote: Only total usage is shown, not split into prompt/completion; this run total = board summary + subscriptions stage (including the model calls of the subscription check). Old core with no data shows "—".
dsh-github-trending.runs.count: Last {count} runs; older ones are trimmed
dsh-github-trending.runs.dryHint: dry run writes nothing and commits nothing
dsh-github-trending.runs.filterHintSubs: Period / dry-run filters apply to digests only; subscriptions are exempt
dsh-github-trending.runs.legacyHint: Legacy records have no preview copy and use the old hash algorithm, so they cannot be compared with v2 directly.
dsh-github-trending.runs.noChange: Content matches the previous issue; the core produced no new file
dsh-github-trending.runs.release.note: A subscription run only checks subscriptions and renders change documents; it produces no digest and does not merge pending subscription changes.
dsh-github-trending.schedule.periods.value: Daily / Weekly / Monthly (all produced by default, no selection needed)
dsh-github-trending.schedule.source: Driven by the plugin’s own 60 s tick (host schedule is session-local and cannot cover unattended runs)
dsh-github-trending.section.subtitle: Fetch, summarize and commit GitHub Trending (daily / weekly / monthly) into your own repo on a schedule. All content comes from the local core binary.
dsh-github-trending.section.title: GitHub Trending
dsh-github-trending.shell.digest.dek: Look back per period — daily / weekly / monthly; only issues with a saved preview copy can be read.
dsh-github-trending.shell.overview.dek: Periodic boards on a schedule; start with the next run, readiness and the last delivery.
dsh-github-trending.shell.runs.dek: The last 30 runs; expand one for artifacts, errors and logs.
dsh-github-trending.shell.settings.dek: The existing settings page; each section saves on its own.
dsh-github-trending.shell.subscriptions.dek: Repo subscription list, versioned in the data repo; add or remove via the core subscribe command.
dsh-github-trending.shell.update.confirmHint: Reinstalls the plugin; restart DSH to apply
dsh-github-trending.skip.merged: The PR for this date was merged; skipped.
dsh-github-trending.skip.pr-closed: The PR for this date was closed unmerged. Scheduled runs do not reopen it; run manually to reopen.
dsh-github-trending.skip.unchanged: The branch already holds the same artifacts; no new commit.
dsh-github-trending.source.local.hint: installed next to the plugin, exits when done
dsh-github-trending.subs.add.queued: Added {repo}; committed with artifacts on the next run.
dsh-github-trending.subs.add.title: Add a repository
dsh-github-trending.subs.analyze.noSubs: No subscription list (subscriptions.yaml) on the current period branch: the core found no subscriptions on {branch}, so no analysis was generated. Make sure subscriptions are committed to the base branch, then retry.
dsh-github-trending.subs.analyze.noSubsOne: The period branch for this repo has no subscription list (subscriptions.yaml), so it cannot be analyzed alone. Make sure subscriptions are committed to the base branch, then retry.
dsh-github-trending.subs.analyze.skipped: No subscriptions to analyze, or nothing changed — no new analysis generated.
dsh-github-trending.subs.analyze.skippedOne: No new changes for {repo} — no new analysis generated.
dsh-github-trending.subs.cmd.add.hint: Enter · committed with artifacts on the next run
dsh-github-trending.subs.cmd.label: Search or add a repo
dsh-github-trending.subs.cmd.placeholder: Search owner/repo, or type a full repo name to add it
dsh-github-trending.subs.desc: Manage subscribed repos and review weekly change records.
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.empty: This repo has no change log yet; it appears here after the first weekly check.
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.note: Data repo {path} — one section appended per week, newest first; the panel is read-only and never rewrites the text.
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.regen.hint: Regenerating calls the model again and may create a new commit/PR.
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.regen.title: Ignore cache and re-run the model for this volume
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.title: Change log · {repo}
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.warn.failed: Not updated this week (failed); the next run retries.
dsh-github-trending.subs.drawer.warn.rate_limited: Not updated this week (rate limited); the next run retries.
dsh-github-trending.subs.empty.hint: Click "＋ Add repository" and enter owner/repo to add one.
dsh-github-trending.subs.empty.match.hint: Press Esc to clear the search, or try another owner / name.
dsh-github-trending.subs.param.hint: Stage behaviour parameters (per-repo limit, tag fallback, period, etc.) are adjusted in the settings page Subscriptions section.
dsh-github-trending.subs.remove.queued: Removed {repo}; committed with artifacts on the next run.
dsh-github-trending.subs.row.triggerFresh: Available once the repo is committed to the subscription list
dsh-github-trending.subs.search.label: Search repositories
dsh-github-trending.subs.title: Subscriptions
dsh-github-trending.subs.toc.label: On this page
dsh-github-trending.summarize.batchSize.help: Repos per model call; larger batches run faster but make each prompt longer.
dsh-github-trending.summarize.enrich.help: Adds external context before summarizing: repo fetches GitHub topics, readme also excerpts the README. Requires a read-only token.
dsh-github-trending.summarize.enrichNote: Enrich needs a read-only token: enrich=repo/readme is best paired with GITHUB_READ_TOKEN (separate, read-only). In readme mode slow networks may skip some repos when the budget runs out (auto-degrades; the run is unaffected).
dsh-github-trending.summarize.maxRetries.help: Extra retries per failed batch; 0 disables retry, and a batch that still fails follows the degrade policy.
dsh-github-trending.summarize.readmeChars.help: Max README characters excerpted per repo when enrich=readme (longer text is truncated).
dsh-github-trending.summaryLang.coreTooOld: The current core is too old (requires ≥ 0.12.0); the summary language takes effect after upgrading the core. You can pick it now and it will apply once upgraded.
dsh-github-trending.summaryLang.help: Language used for generated digests / release summaries. Follows the host UI language by default; anything other than Chinese/English falls back to Chinese. Requires core ≥ 0.12.0.
dsh-github-trending.summaryLang.label: Summary language
